<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Declare which KV cache managers can safely peek past an EAGLE/MTP candidate boundary and then drop back. Resolve eligible groups consistently across core, Mooncake store, and offloading while preserving the current upstream grouping and offloading policies.

Update contribution documentation and the PR template.

Fixes #50630. This updates the existing PR #51351; no second PR is being opened for the same work.

## Claims

- Exclude managers that cannot rewind their cached state from the core and Mooncake fallback; reject unsupported explicit EAGLE annotations when cache-peek selection is active.
- Respect role-specific managers and wrapped uniform specs.
- Preserve `drop_eagle_group_ids`, current proof-margin calculations, and offloading's explicit-draft-group policy.

## Validation

Ubuntu-22.04 under WSL, Python 3.12.16, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, RTX 3060 12GB; official precompiled vLLM extensions matching upstream base `5689c2790c911a55c75825aac5166305df0b591d`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/test_kv_cache_spec_registry.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  -q --tb=short --disable-warnings
```

Human-run validation on 2026-11-03: **929 passed, 3 failed** in 285.17 seconds, matching the earlier run. The same three failures reproduce with the five changed production files replaced by the upstream base versions: one recurrent-event `block_size` expectation and two parameterizations comparing offload job keys as tuple versus set. They are in unchanged `test_scheduler.py` tests.

The core and Mooncake fallback regression tests both fail without this patch (`eagle_group_ids == {0, 1}` instead of `{0}`) and pass with it.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_correctness -v -s
```

Human-run validation on 2026-11-03: **1 passed** in 357.28 seconds using Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base. GSM8K accuracy: 0.346 without speculative decoding and 0.345 with MTP; 99/100 exact text matches, against a required 81. Both decoding modes use the patched code; these are correctness results, not a measured patch-induced accuracy gain or speedup.

On 2026-11-03, the complete configured pre-commit run for the nine changed files passed under WSL with no `SKIP` setting: `pre-commit run --from-ref 5689c2790c911a55c75825aac5166305df0b591d --to-ref HEAD`. The human rerun has 16 passing hooks, 20 automatically skipped for no matching files, and no failures. This includes Ruff, formatting, mypy, test tethering, and the other applicable hooks. ShellCheck 0.11.0 also passed a separate earlier run against `tools/pre_commit/update-dockerfile-graph.sh`. `git diff --check` passes. Full distributed Mooncake service and other GPU platforms were not evaluated.

Final pre-push validation also included the four updated documentation/template files: `pre-commit run --files` with all 13 changed paths passed with no `SKIP` setting (18 passing hooks, 18 automatically skipped for no matching files, no failures). The nine Python source and test files are unchanged from the human-tested version.

## Details

The old fallback could grant a peek to every group, although only managers capable of dropping the extra matched cache unit can safely use it. The capability defaults to false; full attention and sliding window opt in, while circular-window and recurrent managers remain excluded. The shared resolver uses the same role-specific manager selection as the callers.

Offloading intentionally disables fallback selection because upstream now relies on explicit draft annotations. Mooncake keeps `StoreSpecGroup` and groups by both spec and manager. No dependencies, GPU synchronization, or public serving options are added.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)
